content.text:
<context query="FALLBACK_MODEL_ID HAL Engine failover pull request" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/support-agent-fallback-model-allowlist/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.97" tokens="381">
# Fallback Model Allowlist

Adding a fallback table row requires naming 004's recommendation, the fallback vendor's Article 21 assessment, and the failover rows of the zero-retention and transfer-basis documents, with the `evidence` string copied from the fallback assessment's Allowlist row.

Any future `HalEngineConfig` field carrying a `ProviderConfig` extends the resolver's input type.

The `api.model` startup log line includes a `fallback` block with `providerType`, `model`, and `region` when a fallback model is configured; a nested object whose string values are not on the logger-safe key allowlist is dropped rather than logged.

The provider block hands HAL Engine the resolved fallback as the only entry of `fallbackProviders`, the one setting HAL Engine fails over through, and an empty list while `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` is unset, so the fallback the `api.model` line names is the one HAL Engine tries when the primary is unavailable. (#474)

Only the mock row can be a fallback until a fallback vendor is chosen (KU-07): building a real fallback needs that vendor's own settings, so a `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` naming any other row is refused at startup with a message naming `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID`, the id, its provider type and KU-07. (#474)

The mock is refused at startup as the fallback of a `MODEL_ID` that is not the mock: it echoes each customer's own message back as the answer, so behind a real model it would turn that model's outage into answers that pass for success, where the agent must hand off. (#474)

</document>
</section>
